note: What the required CI gate must contain, and what every OTHER workflow in this repository is for. Read from a file so the merge-base ratchet can see it: held as module constants, a job could be excused or a step deleted in the same commit that did it.

not_required.build: it IS the gate; a job cannot require itself

ci.yml.why: the audited one. `build` is the required context and every job here is in its `needs` or waived above.

pr-policy.yml.why: the pull-request BODY check, split out of ci.yml on 2026-09-18 so that editing a description re-runs this and not a 23-minute macOS test job. `gates_merges` is FALSE because it is true of the ruleset, not of the intent: the branch ruleset requires build, compile and test, and `pr-policy` is required by nothing until an administrator adds the context. The duplicate in ci.yml stays until then -- removing it first would delete the merge block and leave a green check that stops nothing. When the context is observed required, this flips and the ci.yml job goes.

maintenance.yml.why: roadmap and ADR-index status against GitHub issues. Moved out of `ci.yml` on 2026-09-18: it is bookkeeping about the project rather than a property of the code a pull request changes, and inside the gate a stale row blocked merges that had not touched the roadmap. It still fails; it no longer blocks.

canon-issue.yml.why: runs on `issues`. There is no merge to block and no `build` job; it comments rather than fails, and that is its whole contract.

release.yml.why: runs on a tag. It gates a RELEASE, not a merge, and its own ordering is what protects that.

publish-mcp.yml.why: publishes registry metadata after a release exists. Nothing about a pull request.

commitlore-preserve.yml.why: runs on `pull_request_target: closed` and only when merged. It preserves records after the fact; there is nothing left to block.
